harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Restricted cron scheduling on node1 to root and opsadmin only via /etc/cron.allow, removed the stale empty /etc/cron.deny, created the opsadmin user, verified enforcement (denyuser blocked, root/opsadmin allowed), cleaned up test artifacts, then performed the mandatory single-node restart with pre/post boot-identity and service-health proof.
actions_performed: Inspected node1 OS/cron setup and confirmed cronie with no pre-existing /etc/cron.allow and an empty /etc/cron.deny
Created opsadmin user (useradd -m)
Confirmed no other non-system users had existing crontabs
Wrote /etc/cron.allow containing root and opsadmin, removed /etc/cron.deny
Created a temporary denyuser to prove enforcement: root and opsadmin could create crontabs via crontab as themselves, denyuser was rejected with 'not allowed to use this program'
Cleaned up test crontabs for root/opsadmin and removed denyuser
Captured pre-restart baseline: boot_id, crond active, cron.allow contents, absence of cron.deny, opsadmin existence
Triggered a safe backgrounded reboot on node1 that let the acknowledgement return before disconnection
Polled node1 until exec was available again
Confirmed boot_id changed and uptime reset to ~0 min, proving an actual restart
Verified post-restart recovery: crond active, cron.allow intact (root, opsadmin), no cron.deny, opsadmin user present, and opsadmin could successfully create/list/remove a crontab entry

evidence.summary: cronie active, no /etc/cron.allow, empty /etc/cron.deny, opsadmin did not yet exist, no existing non-system crontabs
useradd -m opsadmin succeeded; id shows uid=1000(opsadmin)

evidence.requirement: cron.allow restricts scheduling to root and opsadmin
evidence.summary: /etc/cron.allow written with root and opsadmin; /etc/cron.deny removed

evidence.requirement: Enforcement proof: only root/opsadmin can use crontab, others denied
evidence.summary: runuser as root and opsadmin succeeded creating a crontab entry (RC=0 each); runuser as denyuser was rejected with 'You (denyuser) are not allowed to use this program (crontab)' (RC=1)
Test crontabs for root and opsadmin removed, denyuser deleted, cron.allow confirmed intact with root and opsadmin

evidence.requirement: Pre-restart healthy baseline (boot identity + service health)
evidence.summary: boot_id=49dafad6-5cc2-457a-b0f6-1219740a651e captured; crond active; cron.allow=root,opsadmin; no cron.deny; opsadmin exists
Backgrounded 'sleep 2 && reboot' launched; REBOOT_TRIGGERED returned immediately, before the node went down

evidence.requirement: Node restart proof via changed boot identity
evidence.summary: First poll timed out (node down mid-reboot); second poll succeeded with new boot_id=5ca71d65-6d3f-4d05-97b2-a1c6de305a99 (differs from baseline) and uptime '0 min', proving an actual restart occurred

evidence.requirement: Post-restart recovery of cron access control and required services/data
evidence.summary: crond active again, /etc/cron.allow persisted with root/opsadmin, no cron.deny, opsadmin user intact, and opsadmin successfully created/listed a crontab entry post-reboot, then it was cleaned up

attempts.summary: Restricted cron scheduling on node1 to root and opsadmin only via /etc/cron.allow, removed the stale empty /etc/cron.deny, created the opsadmin user, verified enforcement (denyuser blocked, root/opsadmin allowed), cleaned up test artifacts, then performed the mandatory single-node restart with pre/post boot-identity and service-health proof.
